title: Choosing workforce management software for B2B support teams | Pylon
summary: Workforce management software helps support teams forecast demand and optimize scheduling while meeting SLAs. Learn about key features for B2B teams.
body_markdown:
Workforce management (WFM) is how you make sure your team has enough support capacity to meet customer demand. This process helps you avoid two extremes: high labor costs from too many hires and ticket backlogs or falling service levels from not enough coverage.


Dedicated WFM tools can be designed for broad use, focusing mainly on time and attendance. More purpose-built tools may prioritize contact center operations or modern B2B support needs. Some also[offer agentic features](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/agentic-ai-use-cases) that help you move toward blended, efficient human and AI-powered support workflows.


In this article, we’ll walk you through the different types of workforce management software for support teams, and explain what modern B2B teams should look for.


## What are the types of workforce management software?


These are five common kinds of WFM applications. Some workforce management platforms focus mostly on one of these areas, while others offer features in multiple categories.


Type of software How it works Who it's for


Time and attendance WFM Tracks each team member's hours, including overtime and PTO HR and operations teams managing hourly employees


Employee scheduling WFM Helps you build employee schedules and continuously update them to avoid overstaffing or understaffing Team leaders trying to optimize staffing levels and skill mix across shifts


Contact center WFM Creates call volume forecasts and calculates how many team members you need at different times Call centers with high volumes of customer interactions


Support-focused WFM Uses data from different channels to forecast workload and help support team leaders adjust team capacity to meet demand Support teams that work across multiple communication channels like email, Slack, Teams, and live chat


Human plus AI WFM Builds forecasts by estimating how much of future ticket volume can be handled by[AI agents](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-use-ai-agents) , then allocating the remaining workload to your team Customer support teams that make extensive use of agentic AI and automation


## Which kind of WFM software should you choose?


Account custom fields view from Pylon


To choose the best workforce management tool, start by reviewing your team’s operational model and the main challenges you face. Then, look for a platform that helps you overcome those challenges, while letting you keep the parts of your support model that already work well.


For example, if you run a[B2B support team](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/b2b-customer-service-best-practices-strategies) that offers support across channels, you could struggle to forecast workloads accurately using data from siloed tools. To improve planning, you’d benefit from a support-focused tool with strong AI workforce management capabilities.


Here’s when each type of WFM software could fit:


- **Choose time and attendance WFM** if your main challenge is tracking your team’s hours, overtime, leave, and absences.
- **Choose employee scheduling WFM** if you already understand your workload, but you struggle to schedule shifts to ensure sufficient coverage and a good mix of skills.
- **Choose contact center WFM** if you manage a traditional high-volume contact center, and you need to forecast call volumes and schedule teams to[meet SLA targets](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/sla-best-practices) .
- **Choose support-focused WFM** if you manage a B2B customer support team, and your challenges include understanding volumes across channels and making sure you have enough team members for handoffs and escalations on complex issues.
- **Choose human plus AI WFM** if you want to streamline work and improve outcomes using AI agents, and you need to account for agent-handled work when forecasting capacity.


### How to compare WFM options


Once you know the type of workforce management software you need, here’s what to look for in each platform:


- **Startup requirements.** Know how much time and investment you’ll need to set up and configure the new platform.
- **Forecasting tools.** Find out how the platform builds forecasts and what data it uses. B2B support teams need a solution that accounts for handoffs, escalations, and issues with different levels of complexity.
- **Supported channels.** Make sure the app supports the channels your customers use, and pulls in data reliably from all those places.
- **Scheduling features.** Decide if the scheduling depth matches your needs. Some teams just want the right number of team members in place, whereas others prefer detailed scheduling that[takes skills and experience](http://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-agent-skills) into account.
- **Real-time visibility.** Choose a platform that gives you real-time updates on current workload and capacity, so you can spot problems and deal with them fast.
- **Scenario modeling.** The best workforce management tools let you ask “What if?” questions and see the impact of different scenarios. For example, you could see how a 10% spike in ticket volumes might affect your team’s capacity.
- **Third-party integrations.** Be sure your WFM software can use data from your[support software](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/support-software-why-pylon-2026) and operational systems, so you don’t need to move information manually.
- **Scalability.** The system you pick should handle higher volumes and more complex[support workflows](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/support-workflow) as your team scales.


### Common mistakes to avoid


As you compare options, watch out for these pitfalls:


- **Opting for a generic tool.** A WFM application can have strong features, but still cause problems if it doesn’t fit your operating model. For example, a generic time and attendance-tracking system could be great for an HR team, but too rigid for a dynamic B2B environment where demand fluctuates and customer issues vary in complexity.
- **Failing to account for AI.** When AI agents start to handle more customer issues, they don’t always lower the human workload in direct proportion. Agents often have to escalate tickets to your team or wait for approval before taking actions. So you’ll need a sophisticated workforce planning system that calculates the impact of AI accurately.

## FAQ


### What are the biggest challenges in workforce management?


One hard part of workforce management is accurately forecasting demand as ticket volumes change. It can also be challenging to account for AI ticket resolution, especially if you use a traditional model based only on human activity.


### How often should workforce forecasts be updated?


Workforce management is a continuous process, and forecasts should be updated in real time. You’ll need WFM software that gives you a current view of demand and capacity, so you can make adjustments as needed.


### What data does workforce management software use for forecasting?


WFM software uses historical ticket volumes combined with response and resolution times to predict future demand. Some tools can also consider seasonal patterns, and break down overall ticket volume by channel and issue type. Pylon goes even further by using agent resolution and escalation rates to predict AI and human workloads accurately.


### How do you measure whether workforce management is effective?


To see if your WFM process works well, measure outcomes like customer satisfaction and ticket backlog alongside your team’s utilization rate and labor costs. If you can[keep customers happy](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/blog-customer-success-platforms-guide) and manage the queue with minimal friction, all while avoiding excess capacity, your workforce planning is effective.
